newsitem.title: USA: Youth Service chair resigns after placement.
newsitem.headline: Youth Service chair resigns after placement.

text.p: Youth Services International Inc said on Tuesday its chairman and founder W. James Hindman resigned after the company completed the resale of 1.5 million common shares held by Hindman and Henry Felton.
The board named Timothy Cole, chief executive officer, as chairman, it said. The company said last year Hindman would be less active in day-to-day affairs after Cole became ceo.
Felton retired as company president in December.
Gilder, Gagnon, Howe & Co of New York was the placement agent for the selling shareholders.
Hindman still owned about 9.3 percent of the outstanding Youth Services stock, the company said.
Youth Services International operates 21 residential and community based educational and behavioral-change programs for about 3,000 youths in 12 states.
